clue.text: Sensual as a Dahlberg myth

definitions.meaning: sensual means fleshly, of bodily appetites

explanation.surface: Someone describes a sensual quality as being like one of Edward Dahlberg's myths.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnal is a straight synonym of sensual, and the word also forms the title of Dahlberg's book The Carnal Myth.

clue.text: Late offering of Holmes might be as cook prepared

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A late Sherlock Holmes story might read like something a cook has prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' is a link. The Case-Book of Sherlock Holmes (1927) was Conan Doyle's last collection of Holmes stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The Case-Book of Sherlock Holmes was the final volume of Holmes stories, a late offering from the detective's creator.

clue.text: New edition concerning child

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
issue means offspring, a child

explanation.surface: A new edition of a book concerning a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A book brought out again is published a second time, a fresh printing or edition.

clue.text: Queen Anne died despite Johnson's "most universal genius"

definitions.meaning: John ... was Queen Anne's physician, so the queen died in spite of his care
Samuel Johnson called the Scottish doctor and satirist ... the most universal genius of his age

explanation.surface: The queen died even though she had the services of a man Johnson praised as a universal genius.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctor who attended Queen Anne and wrote the John Bull pamphlets is the man Johnson praised so highly.

clue.text: Steadfast song of Greek chorus

parts.note: a choral ode in Greek tragedy sung after the chorus has taken its place; its Greek name means stationary, hence steadfast

explanation.surface: A loyal anthem sung by a chorus in ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek tragedy the stationary ode, sung once the chorus stood in place, takes its name from the Greek for standing still.

clue.text: Said to be epicene character of Jonson

definitions.text: Said to be epicene character of Jonson

parts.words: Said to be epicene character of Jonson
parts.note: Ben Jonson's comedy Epicoene has a subtitle naming the title character, a boy disguised as a quiet bride

explanation.surface: A Jonson character who is reputedly of indeterminate sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Epicoene, or The Silent Woman: the bride Morose marries for her quietness turns out to be a boy, so the character is literally epicene.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonson's play Epicoene carries this alternative title, naming the supposedly mute bride who is really a boy.

clue.text: Yeats saw them as wild, pale, between Saturday and Sunday

indicators.note: between means the word for pale sits inside the two day abbreviations

parts.note: S is a common abbreviation for Saturday
wan means pale

explanation.surface: Yeats saw something wild and pale over the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeats's poem The Wild Swans at Coole names the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeats's collection The Wild Swans at Coole pictures the birds as wild creatures on the lake.

clue.text: Wilde said that such people are wildly unreasonable

definitions.text: Wilde said that such people are wildly unreasonable

parts.words: Wilde said that such people are wildly unreasonable
parts.note: in An Ideal Husband Wilde has Lady Markby say that people fond of music are absurdly unreasonable, wanting silence just when one longs to be deaf

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde remarked on one kind of person being wildly unreasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes people devoted to music, the sort Wilde's character found absurdly demanding.

clue.text: Characteristic of Sir Hercules at Crome overlooked by many

definitions.text: Characteristic of Sir Hercules at Crome overlooked by many

parts.words: Characteristic of Sir Hercules at Crome overlooked by many
parts.note: in Huxley's Crome Yellow Sir Hercules Lapith is a dwarf, and someone very short is literally looked over by most people

explanation.surface: A trait of a character in Huxley's novel that most people fail to notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooked' pretends to mean ignored, but a very short person is physically looked over.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwarfism is the medical term for being abnormally small, the defining trait of Huxley's Sir Hercules.

clue.text: Beckett's dramatic record

parts.note: Samuel Beckett's one-act play in which an old man listens to a tape recording he made decades before

explanation.surface: A play by Beckett, or a recording of his drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' is both the play's subject, a spool of tape, and a sense of a written account.
explanation.definitionFit: Beckett's play centres on a reel-to-reel recording, a record in the literal sense, staged as drama.

clue.text: Mrs H. Manners, novelist

parts.note: the Victorian poet published his novel A Year's Letters under the pen name Mrs Horace Manners

explanation.surface: A lady novelist named in a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: The female name hides a male poet: Algernon Charles Swinburne serialised his novel under this pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet behind the pseudonym Mrs Horace Manners serialised his novel A Year's Letters under it.

clue.text: A new boy representing one whose voyage O'Brian recorded

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A new boy at school plays the part of an explorer from Patrick O'Brian's book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representing' is a link. Patrick O'Brian's novels The Golden Ocean and The Unknown Shore follow Commodore George Anson's voyage round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Commodore George Anson led the 1740s circumnavigation that O'Brian retold in two early novels.

clue.text: Shelter offered by Inge

parts.note: William Inge's play is set in a roadside diner where coach passengers wait out a snowstorm

explanation.surface: A refuge provided by the playwright Inge.
explanation.definitionFit: Inge's play takes its title from a roadside halt where travellers shelter, much like a covered stop for coaches.

clue.text: "We are over-run with a race of vermin they call wits, a generation of —— that are always making a noise." (Thomas Otway, The Atheist)

definitions.text: "We are over-run with a race of vermin they call wits, a generation of —— that are always making a noise." (Thomas Otway, The Atheist)

parts.words: "We are over-run with a race of vermin they call wits, a generation of —— that are always making a noise." (Thomas Otway, The Atheist)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Otway likens noisy wits to small buzzing creatures, following on from vermin

explanation.surface: A line from Otway's play complaining about noisy wits.
explanation.definitionFit: Small buzzing creatures fit the gap, continuing Otway's picture of the wits as vermin always making a noise.

clue.text: Young poem intended to be pacific, say?

definitions.meaning: Edward Young, of Night Thoughts: An Ode
the Pacific is an example of a great sea, and the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: A poem by Young that was meant to be peaceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Young wrote Ocean: An Ode, and the Pacific is the largest of the great seas.

clue.text: Manipulative character in old-hat novel

parts.note: George du Maurier's novel Trilby shares its name with a soft felt hat, and its villain is the hypnotist who controls the heroine

explanation.surface: A scheming figure in a dated, old-fashioned book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-hat' seems to mean dated, but points to Trilby, both a novel (1894) and a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Du Maurier's hypnotist who controls Trilby has become a byword for anyone who manipulates another.

clue.text: Joyce Carol Oates distinguished them from other women

definitions.text: Joyce Carol Oates distinguished them from other women

parts.words: Joyce Carol Oates distinguished them from other women
parts.note: Oates's story collection is titled The Goddess and Other Women, setting divine females apart from the rest

explanation.surface: The novelist Oates made a distinction between certain women and the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Oates's collection title sets divine female figures apart from ordinary women.

clue.text: In favour of chic for Greek portico

parts.note: pro means in favour of
style means chic, elegance

explanation.surface: Someone approves of a stylish portico in the Greek manner.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical architecture the term names a portico or temple front with free-standing columns across the front only.

clue.text: One was made when Dedalus was young

definitions.text: One was made when Dedalus was young

parts.words: One was made when Dedalus was young
parts.note: Joyce's novel A ... of the Artist as a Young Man depicts Stephen Dedalus in his youth

explanation.surface: Something was created during Dedalus's youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce's novel is a likeness of Stephen Dedalus painted in words as a young man.

clue.text: Idle Thoughts Of an Idle Fellow in the Russian novel?

definitions.text: Idle Thoughts Of an Idle Fellow in the Russian novel?

parts.words: Idle Thoughts Of an Idle Fellow in the Russian novel?
parts.note: Jerome K. Jerome's book title is borrowed to describe Goncharov's Russian hero, the byword for idleness who barely leaves his bed

explanation.surface: Jerome's Idle Thoughts of an Idle Fellow, as told in a Russian book.
explanation.definitionFit: Goncharov's title character, the archetype of Russian sloth, is the idle fellow of Russian fiction.

clue.text: One with a gift for opening dramas, operas — new, or rewrites

indicators.note: opening means the first letters of the three following words are taken

explanation.surface: A benefactor funds the opening of new dramas and operas, or perhaps their rewrites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' takes D, O and N from dramas, operas, new, and OR follows as written; 'rewrites' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives money or an organ is a giver, a person who bestows a gift.

clue.text: Normal, like Cumberland's son?

definitions.meaning: normal means ordinary, as in the course of nature
Richard Cumberland's comedy is titled The ... Son, meaning one born out of wedlock

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is normal to be like the son of Cumberland.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal and unaffected are senses of the word, and an illegitimate child was once a natural son, as in Cumberland's play.

clue.text: Which journalist's novels and reviews were little gems?

definitions.meaning: James Agate, the drama critic, also wrote novels; his works are the journalist's

explanation.surface: Asking which journalist wrote novels and reviews that were small masterpieces.
explanation.definitionFit: James Agate was a critic and novelist, and agates are banded chalcedony stones used as small gems.

clue.text: Patience rewarded him, and his collaborator

definitions.text: Patience rewarded him, and his collaborator

parts.words: Patience rewarded him, and his collaborator
parts.note: the comic opera Patience was a success for its librettist and his composer partner Sullivan

explanation.surface: Being patient paid off for a man and his partner.
explanation.definitionFit: W. S. Gilbert wrote the words for Patience, which Arthur Sullivan set to music, and both profited.

clue.text: Sort of script favoured by Lamb?

definitions.text: Sort of script favoured by Lamb?

parts.words: Sort of script favoured by Lamb?
parts.note: Charles Lamb wrote essays as Elia, so writing in his manner is named after that pen name

explanation.surface: A kind of handwriting Charles Lamb preferred.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective formed from Elia, Lamb's pen name, describes anything in the style of his essays.

clue.text: So terse a version of matricide

indicators.note: a version of says the letters are presented in another form or order

explanation.surface: A brief account of a mother-murder, so terse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matricide' here means the person who kills his mother, not the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the son of Agamemnon killed his mother Clytemnestra, making him a mother-slayer.

clue.text: What scores indicate (some times)

definitions.meaning: musical scores mark the speeds at which passages are played
the musical speeds are plural of a word for time or pace

explanation.surface: Something that music scores mark, at certain moments.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeds of musical performance, plural of the Italian word for time, are marked in printed music.

clue.text: Bridges work somehow bares a spy in casual pedestrian

indicators.note: somehow says the letters fall into place in some other way

explanation.surface: A poem by Bridges in which a spy is unmasked as someone strolling past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridges work' also defines it: Robert Bridges wrote the poem A Passer-By.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone walking by by chance, not stopping, is a casual pedestrian.

clue.text: Beerbohm made them all going on board with the king

definitions.text: Beerbohm made them all going on board with the king

parts.words: Beerbohm made them all going on board with the king
parts.note: Max Beerbohm's book of stories about imaginary writers is titled with a number of people

explanation.surface: Beerbohm created a group of people who all boarded a ship with the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Beerbohm's 1919 book of fictional literary portraits is named for its group of characters.

clue.text: Unfaithful wife to mark, say

parts.note: in the legend King Mark of Cornwall's bride betrayed him with Tristan

explanation.surface: Someone notes an unfaithful wife, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mark' looks like a verb; it is King Mark of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Tristan legend King Mark's bride loves Tristan, making her an adulterous queen.
